title: Proper-direct-image product comparison is inverse to compact-support Kunneth
statement:
Use the finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ and normalized geometric constructible operations of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. Let $p_i:X_i\to Y_i$ for $i=1,2$ be proper morphisms of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $p=p_1\times_kp_2$, and let $M_i\in D^b_{ctf}(X_i,A)$. Write $r_i:X_1\times_kX_2\to X_i$ and $s_i:Y_1\times_kY_2\to Y_i$ for the projections. Let $\alpha_i:s_i^*Rp_{i*}M_i\to Rp_*r_i^*M_i$ be the ordinary exchange maps of these projection squares and $t_p:Rp_*B\otimes Rp_*C\to Rp_*(B\otimes C)$ the usual lax tensor map, the ordinary-adjunction transpose of the tensor of the two pullback counits. Define
$$\Pi^p_{M_1,M_2}:Rp_{1*}M_1\boxtimes Rp_{2*}M_2\xrightarrow{\alpha_1\otimes\alpha_2}Rp_*r_1^*M_1\otimes Rp_*r_2^*M_2\xrightarrow{t_p}Rp_*(M_1\boxtimes M_2).$$
With $R(-)_!=R(-)_*$ identified by the specified proper compactification, this is exactly $\mathrm{Ku}_!^{-1}$ for the compact-support Kunneth isomorphism of [def-sf-kv-maps](i). In particular it is an isomorphism with those canonical maps, not merely an unspecified isomorphism of the same objects. For the proper-direct-image comparison induced by a proper morphism of correspondences in [lem-trf-proper-direct-image-comparison], its map $\Pi$ of [def-trf-cohomological-comparison] is this $\Pi^p$ with $p_1=p_2=p_X$.

source.place: §4.1.4(a), Notation 4.2.3(ii); normalization of the product map against the compact-support Kunneth construction

proof.text:
Use $T=Y_1\times_kY_2$, $U=X_1\times_kY_2$, $V=Y_1\times_kX_2$, $u=p_1\times1$, $v=1\times p_2$, and $W=U\times_TV=X_1\times_kX_2$. Write $a_1:U\to X_1$, $a_2:V\to X_2$, $j_1:W\to U$, $j_2:W\to V$ for the projections, so $p=uj_1=vj_2$ and $r_i=a_ij_i$. Put $K_1=La_1^*M_1$, $K_2=La_2^*M_2$. The maps $u,v$ are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], being base changes of $p_i$. The base $T$ is separated finite type and the $K_i$ are finite-Tor constructible, as required in the construction of [def-sf-kv-maps](i). Let $e_1:Ls_1^*Rp_{1*}M_1\to Ru_*K_1$ and $e_2:Ls_2^*Rp_{2*}M_2\to Rv_*K_2$ be exchange for the Cartesian squares $(a_1,u,p_1,s_1)$ and $(a_2,v,p_2,s_2)$. With the proper compactifications $j=1$, [def-exchange-projection] defines these as the compact-support exchanges as well. In the notation of [thm-sf-kunneth-relative], let $\kappa=\kappa_{u,v}$. Then the definition gives exactly
$$\mathrm{Ku}_!^{-1}=\kappa^{-1}\circ(e_1\otimes_A^Le_2).$$
All the maps in this construction are isomorphisms, with $!$ identified with $*$ as in [prop-functor-package](3).

source.place: Evaluation (1), paragraph beginning “Indeed”: inverse product characterized by the tensor of ordinary pullback counits

proof.text:
Put $H_i=Ls_i^*Rp_{i*}M_i$, $Q_i=Lr_i^*M_i$, and $F_i=Lr_i^*\varepsilon_{p_i,M_i}:Lp^*H_i\to Q_i$, inserting the canonical pullback composition and monoidal identifications of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. The ordinary exchange $\alpha_i:H_i\to Rp_*Q_i$ of the commutative square $p_ir_i=s_ip$ means the mate of $F_i$ under [fix-prop-adjunctions](1): explicitly
$$\alpha_i=Rp_*(F_i)\circ\eta_{p,H_i},\qquad \varepsilon_{p,Q_i}\circ Lp^*\alpha_i=F_i.$$
The second equality is naturality of $\varepsilon_p$ followed by $\varepsilon_p Lp^*\circ Lp^*\eta_p=1$. These squares need not be Cartesian; only the two squares defining $e_i$ in Step 1 are being used as Cartesian exchange squares. By the defining transpose of $t_p$ and tensor functoriality,
$$\varepsilon_{p,Q_1\otimes Q_2}\circ Lp^*\bigl(t_p(\alpha_1\otimes\alpha_2)\bigr)
=(\varepsilon_{p,Q_1}\circ Lp^*\alpha_1)\otimes(\varepsilon_{p,Q_2}\circ Lp^*\alpha_2)=F_1\otimes F_2.$$
Thus this is the ordinary transpose of the map $\Pi^p$ in the statement.

source.place: §0.3(b), formula (0.1); ordinary adjunction calculation for commutative product squares

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-relative-kunneth-counit] to the proper maps $u,v$ and the objects $K_1,K_2$ of Step 1. Its equality is
$$\varepsilon_p\circ Lp^*\kappa^{-1}=Lj_1^*\varepsilon_{u,K_1}\otimes Lj_2^*\varepsilon_{v,K_2}.$$
By [def-exchange-projection], the transposes of $e_1,e_2$ give
$$\varepsilon_{u,K_1}\circ Lu^*e_1=La_1^*\varepsilon_{p_1,M_1},\qquad
\varepsilon_{v,K_2}\circ Lv^*e_2=La_2^*\varepsilon_{p_2,M_2}.$$
Precompose the first displayed equality with $Lp^*(e_1\otimes e_2)$ and use $p=uj_1=vj_2$. Its right side becomes
$Lj_1^*(\varepsilon_u\circ Lu^*e_1)\otimes Lj_2^*(\varepsilon_v\circ Lv^*e_2)=F_1\otimes F_2$.
This calculates the transpose of $\mathrm{Ku}_!^{-1}$ itself, using exactly the Cartesian exchanges in its definition. The pullback and tensor identifications are those of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso].

source.place: Evaluation (1), paragraph beginning “Indeed”: inverse product characterized by the tensor of ordinary pullback counits

proof.text: Steps 2 and 3 give equal transposes for $\Pi^p$ and $\mathrm{Ku}_!^{-1}$ with the same source $H_1\otimes H_2$ and target $Rp_*(Q_1\otimes Q_2)$. The adjunction bijection of [fix-prop-adjunctions](1) therefore makes these maps equal. The latter is an isomorphism by [def-sf-kv-maps](i), proving the canonical-map assertion and invertibility.

source.place: Evaluation (1), paragraph beginning “Indeed”: inverse product characterized by the tensor of ordinary pullback counits

proof.text:
For a proper pushforward diagram of [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward], [lem-trf-proper-direct-image-comparison] specifies $f_X=Rp_{X*}$, $f_{X\times X}=R(p_X\times p_X)_*$ and the usual lax tensor map, together with the ordinary mates for all the commutative fixed-diagram squares; no Cartesian hypothesis on these squares is imposed. Distinguish the product projections $\operatorname{pr}_i$ from the two proper maps $p_i$ used earlier. The formula in [def-trf-cohomological-comparison] is
$$\Pi_{M,N}=t_{X\times X}\circ(\alpha_{\operatorname{pr}_1}\otimes\alpha_{\operatorname{pr}_2}).$$
Here $\alpha_{\operatorname{pr}_i}$ is the mate of $L\operatorname{pr}_i^*\varepsilon_{p_X}$. Taking $p_1=p_2=p_X$ in Step 2 gives these very mates and this very lax tensor map. Hence the prescribed $\Pi$ is exactly $\Pi^p$, without changing any map or coefficient domain.

proof_origin.place: Evaluation (1), paragraph beginning “Indeed”: inverse product characterized by the tensor of ordinary pullback counits; expanded using the existing relative-counit lemma and ordinary adjunctions. Varshavsky §§0.3(b), 4.1.4(a), 4.2.3(ii) prescribe the tensor and comparison maps, not this Kunneth identification.
